To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a systems biology approach identified a network model that can explain the relationship between muscle response to training, systemic inflammatory mediators and skeletal muscle abnormalities in COPD.

(i) COPD muscle dysfunction is associated with a failure to coordinate the expression of tissue remodelling genes, (ii) this failure is associated with a specific pattern of altered expression of histone modifiers and (iii) the altered expression of histones modifiers is associated with altered muscle oxygen utilization.
a network biology approach can be used to model the relationship of muscle molecular and physiological responses to training and systemic inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the skeletal muscle dysfunction in COPD patients and with developing new strategies for the treatment of these patients.
the application of systems biology tools to the study of skeletal muscle in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
understanding how COPD patients’ muscles are affected by systemic inflammation and how they respond to exercise training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
COPD patients have an abnormal expression of several genes and molecular pathways that may contribute to the development of muscle wasting and weakness.
COPD patients have an abnormal skeletal muscle phenotype that is characterized by a failure in the co-ordinate activation of tissue remodelling pathways.
COPD muscle dysfunction is the result of the combined effects of a systemic inflammatory response and a hypoxic stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a systems biology approach is able to identify the key players involved in muscle remodelling in COPD, and may be useful for the development of novel therapies.
the failure to co-ordinate the expression of tissue remodelling pathways in response to training is a key molecular signature of skeletal muscle abnormalities in COPD.
COPD is a systemic disease, with a specific molecular signature of skeletal muscles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of a network biology approach may be a powerful tool to identify novel molecular targets for the treatment of muscle abnormalities in COPD.
network biology approaches may be used to identify novel disease mechanisms and to guide the design of new therapeutic interventions.
network analysis can be successfully used to model and predict the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of complex diseases.
